neighbours.label: quantum physics: its phenomena and founders (superposition, entanglement, uncertainty, tunnelling, wave-particle duality, Heisenberg, Bohr, Planck); classical physics described in the same frames stays low
fire: Quantum computers use qubits that hold many states at once.
Measuring one entangled photon instantly fixes the state of its partner.
Heisenberg showed that position and momentum cannot both be known exactly.
Electrons tunnel through barriers they classically could not cross.
Bohr and Einstein argued about quantum theory for decades.
In the double-slit experiment, single electrons form an interference pattern.
Planck proposed that energy comes in discrete quanta.
Her startup sells software for quantum chemistry.
quiet: Supercomputers use thousands of ordinary processors at once.
Measuring the speed of one car tells you nothing about the next.
Newton showed that the same force pulls apples and the Moon.
Water flows through pipes faster when they are wider.
Bohr and Einstein both enjoyed long walks.
In the wind tunnel, smoke shows the flow over the wing.
Kepler proposed that planets move in ellipses.
Her startup sells software for restaurant bookings.
